intro: Hi! I am Md Mosharaf Hossan, but you’ll mostly meet me as mosharaf13 on the internet.
aboutMe:
I am an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, specializing in game systems, mixed reality, and full-stack software development. I completed my M.S. in Computer Science at Idaho State University (GPA: 3.96), where my research focused on developing gamified VR based interventions to help individuals with Mysophobia based OCD manage their symptoms. 

 My research integrates virtual reality games with biofeedback. I have published multiple peer-reviewed papers at IEEE venues including COMPSAC, IETC, IoTaIS, and MSR, with recognitions such as the Premium Paper Award (IETC 2025) and Best Paper Award (IETC 2024). My primary work explores adaptive VR exposure therapy using real-time heart rate feedback.
outro:
As an educator, I teach courses related to Game Systems, Game Engine Architecture, Multiplayer Systems, and Mixed Reality. I mentor students in applying design patterns, DevOps workflows, AI-assisted development, and agile practices to build production-ready interactive systems using Unity, Laravel, and modern full-stack technologies.

 Before academia, I spent over five years in industry as a software engineer and team lead. I helped building enterprise SaaS systems and telecom automation tools. I led Scrum teams, designed high-impact automation systems that reduced operational costs, and delivered large-scale production systems used by thousands of users daily.
